To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the leakage of the Ta2 O5 films is almost two orders lower than that of the SiO 2 films, that the leakage of Ta 2O5 depends on the work function of the metal electrode, that the charge in the oxide near the Si–SiO 2 interface is almost independent on the metal electrode and that the charge near the metal–oxide interface is almost independent of the metal electrode except for Au.
the oxide charge is composed of three contributions: the SiO2/Si interface, the Ta2O 5/SiO 2 interface and the Ta2 O 5 near the metal interface.
the metal–Ta2O5–SiO2–Si structures can be successfully applied for the realization of MOS devices, provided that the metal is W or Au and not Al.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the electrical properties of metal–insulator–semiconductor structures, in which the insulator layer is a thin Ta2O5 film.

the development of a comprehensive model for I(V) and C(V) characteristics of metal–insulator–semiconductor (MIS) structures containing a Ta2O5 layer and the influence of the metal on the leakage and on the oxide charges.
the study of the influence of different metals on the conduction and the charge properties of metal–insulator–semiconductor structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the metal–insulator–semiconductor structure with W top electrode and Ta2O5 insulator is the most suitable for the application in metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) and metal–oxide–silicon capacitors.
for the studied structures the following sequence of the leakage currents is valid: Al > W > Au, while the sequence of the flatband voltage shift is the reverse: Au > W > Al.
the best metal–insulator–semiconductor (MIS) structures for the studied insulator and metal combinations are those with W and Au electrodes, while those with the Al electrode are the worst.

the leakage current in metal–insulator–semiconductor structures with thin insulators is dominated by Poole–Fenkel conduction in the insulator, which is strongly affected by the work function of the metal electrode.
the leakage current in the metal–oxide–silicon structures is mainly governed by the properties of the oxide, while the metal has only a minor effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metal–oxide–silicon system is a very sensitive structure to the metal used, which can be used for a precise control of the oxide charges.
the leakage of the metal–insulator–semiconductor structure can be significantly reduced by using metals of high work function.
the leakage current and the oxide charges can be controlled by the metal used for top electrode.
